messages:
marta: CI linkcheck is red on migration/docs-reorg (PR #591). Multiple broken anchor warnings after we flattened headings in the API reference. Copying excerpt from the job log below. ci-bot: linkcheck: 5 failed links detected - /docs/api/generate#response-format -> 404 (fragment not found) - /docs/api/embed#vector-size -> 404 (fragment not found) - /docs/guide/migration#python-snippets -> 404 (fragment not found) - /docs/console/ops#tokens-per-route -> 404 (fragment not found) - /docs/sdk/js#quickstart -> 200 (ok) but redirected -> warn luke: This smells like heading ID changes from the reorg. Docusaurus/MkDocs slugify rules differ; when we collapsed a level the autogenerated id changed (e.g. "Response format" -> response-format vs responseformat). nidhi: I can reproduce locally with mkdocs-material v8.4. The anchor for headings with parentheses or slashes gets sanitized differently. We should prefer explicit header IDs in the docs where stable anchors are important. Example: ```markdown ## Response format {#response-format} ``` sam: Agreed. For the API reference I prefer to add explicit ids rather than relying on slugify so client links don't break across tool upgrades. Also we should run a small script to reconcile old anchors to new ones and add redirects for the site. marta: Good plan. For the short term can we add a small redirect map in mkdocs.yml? mkdocs-redirects plugin supports a simple mapping. Something like: ```yaml site_dir: site plugins: - redirects: redirects: docs/api/generate#response-format: docs/api/generate#response-format ``` (luke: that example is nonsense haha but you get the idea) luke: I'll open a tiny PR that adds explicit header ids to the three API pages we changed and add a redirects entry for the migration guide. Quick question: do we want breadcrumbs updated too? Some apps link by textual headings elsewhere. nidhi: Breadcrumbs are separate; they're path-based so shouldn't break. But mention it in the PR description so reviewers verify. ci-bot: note: linkcheck job includes a --fragment-check flag; you can re-run per-commit. sam: One gotcha I hit earlier: when a heading starts with an inline code span the slugifier sometimes preserves backticks differently. If you're adding explicit ids it's safer than trying to predict slug behavior. marta: I'll stop the merge and assign this to @luke. @nidhi can you add a small test harness that asserts all internal fragments resolve after build? We currently only run full linkcheck in CI weekly; let's make it per-PR for docs/* changes. nidhi: Yep, I can add a GH action step that runs linkchecker on the built site on PRs touching /docs. Should be fast enough. luke: Opening WIP PR with edits: changes include explicit {#ids} on API headings, a redirects map for the most common anchors, and a note in docs/migration.md about slug differences across generators. Will ping for review when CI is green. marta: Thanks. Once PR lands we should re-run the site build and verify live anchors. If anything else fails we can add HTML anchor tags as a last resort: ```html

Response format

``` sam: Nice. Also adding a tiny entry in the contributor guide about stable anchors and examples to avoid surprises when migrating. :memo: marta: Sounds good. Leaving this open until redirect PR merges.
